answer: Each name must store unique bytes. A joiner draws a sealed shard from a public archival lagoon, tags it with an umber dye (pigment hash of shard and address, void if copied), and parks 1,400 POA for 20 epochs. Each epoch a 70-second audit names fourteen offsets; the key returns a fourteen-line sonnet plus the dye. Miss or collide: slash 450 POA, exile 16 epochs. Honest cost: 1,400 POA and one shard; 1,000 names need 1.4 million POA and 1,000 live shards, vs ~150 POA reward. Risk: one host streams a shard to many keys; cross-cluster audits collide on that dye and slash the set.
